subject: Business
title: Choice Overload: Too Many Options
description: One-minute skill: Choice Overload: Too Many Options.

hook.text: A store displayed 24 jams. Another displayed 6. The small display sold 10x more jam.

buildup.text: Sheena Iyengar proved that too many options paralyze people instead of empowering them.

discovery.text: When overwhelmed, we default to choosing nothing. The brain's shortcut for complexity is avoidance.

twist.text: More options feel better — customers say they want choice — but they actually buy less.

climax.text: Successful menus, apps, and stores curate ruthlessly. They remove options to increase action.

punchline.text: More choice doesn't mean more freedom. Often it means more paralysis.

quiz.question: What did Iyengar's jam experiment show?
options: Fewer options led to more purchases
More options led to more purchases
The type of jam mattered most

details.summary: Choice overload occurs when too many options paralyze decision-making, reduce satisfaction, and increase regret. Sheena Iyengar's famous jam study showed that displays with fewer options generated ten times more purchases than those with extensive variety.
details.whyItMatters: For product designers and retailers, more options do not always mean more sales. Strategic curation of choices increases conversion rates, customer satisfaction, and reduces the cognitive burden that drives shoppers away.
takeaways: Too many options can paralyze consumers and reduce purchase rates
Iyengar's jam study showed 6 options outsold 24 options by tenfold
Curating choices and providing defaults helps customers decide confidently

faq.question: Does choice overload apply to all product categories?
faq.answer: Research shows it is strongest when options are complex, differences are hard to evaluate, and stakes are moderate. For simple commodities or expert buyers with clear preferences, more choice can be beneficial. Context determines whether variety helps or hurts.

faq.question: How can businesses offer variety without causing overload?
faq.answer: Use category filters to break large assortments into manageable groups. Highlight recommended or popular items as defaults. Provide comparison tools that surface meaningful differences. Limit visible options initially with an option to see more on request.
